patient.chief_complaint: Sudden worst headache of life while at gym, vomiting, neck stiffness
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. Clark is a 52-year-old woman with hypertension and smoking who presents with an instantaneous thunderclap headache that began while exercising at the gym, rated 10/10 at onset. She immediately vomited and was helped off the treadmill by staff. She arrived by ambulance 45 minutes later. She has marked neck stiffness and photophobia. No loss of consciousness. No focal deficits. Classic SAH presentation.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4; GCS 15; photophobic; severe pain
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: PERRL 3mm; EOM intact; no papilledema; no CN deficit
neurological_exam.additional: Marked nuchal rigidity; Kernig positive; Hunt-Hess Grade 2

findings.location: Basal cisterns and bilateral Sylvian fissures
findings.description: Thick hyperdense blood in suprasellar cistern and bilateral Sylvian fissures

ct.impression: 1. Subarachnoid hemorrhage, Fisher grade 3, with thick hyperdense blood in the basal cisterns, bilateral Sylvian fissures, and anterior interhemispheric fissure. 2. No intraparenchymal hemorrhage. 3. No hydrocephalus. CTA head and neck recommended for vascular evaluation. Clinical correlation recommended.
recommended_actions: CTA head and neck recommended for vascular evaluation

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: WBC 14.8 x10^9/L (H), Glucose 148 mg/dL (H), Troponin I 0.18 ng/mL (H), BNP 164 pg/mL (H).

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 26 cmH2O. WBC: N/A (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 188 mg/dL. Glucose: 74 mg/dL (serum 148, ratio 0.50) (ratio 0.50). Xanthochromia: Present.

ecg.interpretation: Sinus tachycardia, rate 98. Deep T-wave inversions in V1–V5. QTc mildly prolonged at 486 ms. No ST-segment elevation. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Saccular aneurysm 5.4 x 4.8 mm with irregular morphology and daughter sac

output.impression: 1. Saccular aneurysm of the anterior communicating artery, measuring 5.4 x 4.8 mm, with irregular morphology and a daughter sac. 2. No additional intracranial aneurysms. Findings are consistent with the source of subarachnoid hemorrhage. Conventional DSA recommended for treatment planning. Clinical correlation recommended.
recommended_actions: Conventional DSA recommended for treatment planning

output.impression: Moderate bilateral vasospasm. Bilateral ACA mean flow velocities 138–146 cm/s, Lindegaard ratios 3.8–4.2. Bilateral MCA mean flow velocities 112–122 cm/s. Basilar velocity within normal limits. Clinical correlation recommended.

1. Left ventricular ejection fraction 50%. 2. Mild apical hypokinesis. 3. Mitral and aortic valves are normal. Consider repeat echocardiogram in 6 weeks to assess interval change. Clinical correlation recommended.
recommended_actions: Consider repeat echocardiogram in 6 weeks to assess interval change

output.query: AHA SAH management guidelines nimodipine vasospasm 2023

results.finding: Nimodipine 60 mg q4h x21 days Class I Level A
Triple-H therapy for symptomatic vasospasm - induce hypertension first

output.summary: Oral nimodipine (60 mg every 4 hours for 21 days) is a Class I, Level A recommendation for patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, based on reduction in poor outcomes attributable to delayed cerebral ischemia. Early aneurysm treatment within 24–48 hours is recommended to reduce rebleeding risk. Transcranial Doppler monitoring is widely used for vasospasm surveillance in the days following SAH. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Mild-to-moderate bilateral ACA territory hypoperfusion. Cerebral blood flow mildly-to-moderately reduced (30–36 mL/100g/min). Preserved cerebral blood volume bilaterally, without established infarction. Clinical correlation recommended.

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

cardiac_monitoring.rhythm_summary: Predominant sinus rhythm throughout the recording
findings: Brief runs of asymptomatic sinus tachycardia. No sustained arrhythmia, no pauses greater than 2 seconds, no AV block.
cardiac_monitoring.impression: 24-hour Holter monitor with only benign findings.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from anterior communicating artery aneurysm (Hunt-Hess 2, Fisher 3)

differential.key_features: CT shows blood; CSF diagnostic; CTA shows aneurysm
Saccular aneurysm on CTA; no arterial beading
Bloody CSF not purulent; normal glucose ratio

critical_actions: CTA identifies AComA aneurysm - treat within 24 hours
contraindicated_actions: Do not continue losartan with nimodipine
key_reasoning_points: Classic thunderclap headache during exertion with meningism = textbook SAH
AComA is the most common aneurysm location
Fisher grade 3 predicts moderate-high vasospasm risk
Nimodipine 60 mg q4h x21 days is Level A evidence for vasospasm prevention
Losartan must be held - additive hypotension with nimodipine
